test_title: PYST 47: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held on 10 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom from the following options that can substitute the underlined part of the given sentence.

Sometimes __doing something that makes it impossible to return to the previous situation later__ strengthens you.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3)** i.e. **"Burning your Bridges"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An** Idiom** is a collection of words established by usage as having a meaning distinct from the meanings of the individual words
 
• The above-underlined sentence can be substituted with the Idiom "**Burning your bridges".**
 
• The idiom Burning your bridges means **doing something that makes it impossible to revert to a previous state.**
 
 
• **Example**: By saying those words you burned your bridges.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is "Burning your bridges". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some idioms related to fire are :
 
 
• Fired up - energized, excited, enthusiastic
 
 
• Example: The audience fired up the contestants by cheering for them.
 
 
 
• To play with fire - to take a stupid risk.
 
 
• Example: Messing with the teacher is like playing with fire.
 
 
 
• To breathe fire - To be dangerously angry.
 
 
• Example: You better keep your mouth shut, she is breathing fire right now.
